summary: This article explains how solar panels turn sunlight into electricity, why sunny deserts like parts of Saudi Arabia are ideal locations for solar farms, and the challenges of relying on the sun for power.
introduce: Ask students to share a small problem they solved this week and how they solved it, and write two examples in a Problem | Solution chart on the board. Tell them that “Solar Farms: Power from the Desert Sun” also has a problem and a solution to find.

keyTerms.def: a small part inside a panel that can turn light into electricity
a large group of things set up together in rows
a form of energy that flows through wires and powers lights and machines

challengeTerms.def: describing a material or device that changes light directly into electricity
a special material that can control the flow of electricity, used to make solar cells and computer chips
stopping and starting again; not steady

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that every country should build more solar farms? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the advantages and one problem of solar power.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review cell, array, and electricity, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses photovoltaic, semiconductor, and intermittent to suggest a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
